plan.contextChunk: This figure traces the operation of merge sort on an eight-element array as a bottom-up lattice of gray boxes linked by thick gray arrows. The bottom rank, tagged "initial sequence", holds eight single-element squares reading 5, 2, 4, 7, 1, 3, 2, 6 from left to right. Pairs of arrows, each pair captioned "merge", lift adjacent squares into four two-element boxes reading 2 5, 4 7, 1 3, and 2 6. A second rank of merge arrows combines those into two four-element boxes, 2 4 5 7 and 1 2 3 6. A last pair of arrows, again captioned "merge", brings both into the wide box at the top, tagged "sorted sequence", which reads 1 2 2 3 4 5 6 7. Box width scales with the run it holds, so the doubling of sorted-run length shows up directly as the boxes widen from rank to rank while their count halves. Read upward, the drawing presents the algorithm as repeated merging of already-sorted runs.

interactionPlan.concept: Merge sort builds a sorted array from the bottom up by repeatedly merging pairs of smaller, already-sorted subarrays into larger sorted runs.
elements: Bottom rank: 8 single-element gray squares containing 5, 2, 4, 7, 1, 3, 2, 6
Label 'initial sequence' below the bottom rank
Second rank: 4 two-element gray rectangles containing 2 5, 4 7, 1 3, 2 6
Third rank: 2 four-element gray rectangles containing 2 4 5 7, 1 2 3 6
Top rank: 1 eight-element gray rectangle containing 1 2 2 3 4 5 6 7
Label 'sorted sequence' above the top rank
Thick gray diagonal arrows pointing from each child block to its parent block
Labels 'merge' positioned near the pairs of arrows

interactions.label: Duplicate highlighting
interactions.teaches: By visually distinguishing the two '2's, we can see if the algorithm is stable—that is, whether the '2' that started on the left remains on the left in the final sorted array.

interactions.label: Merge Routine
interactions.teaches: The merge step operates by repeatedly picking the smaller of the front elements from two already-sorted arrays (L and R), resulting in a single combined sorted array.

interactions.success_check: Every parent block is fully populated in sorted order, and the top block contains the fully sorted array.

demo_steps.title: The Merge Process
demo_steps.narration: Merge sort works bottom-up. It treats each element as a sorted run of length 1, then merges adjacent pairs into sorted runs of length 2, 4, and finally 8.

demo_steps.title: Algorithm Stability
demo_steps.narration: Notice the two '2's. A stable sort keeps them in their original order. Using '<=' instead of '<' in the merge condition guarantees the left '2' is taken first when they tie. Try running the buggy code to see stability break!

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Merging two sorted sequences takes only linear time by comparing their front elements; repeating this in a tree structure sorts the entire array.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Layout as a 4-level tree of gray rectangles. Box widths must physically scale with the number of elements they contain (e.g. rank 2 boxes are twice as wide as rank 1 boxes). The generator should initially draw the higher-rank boxes as empty slots; they will populate dynamically as the code_editor's take() operations execute. When 'Highlight duplicates' is active, color the first '2' (from index 1) blue and the second '2' (from index 6) red throughout all levels to track their movement.

discrepancies: The default (step-0) view only displays numbers in the bottom row of boxes (leaving the upper boxes empty), whereas the source figure displays the fully populated tree simultaneously.
The numbers and 'merge' labels use a sans-serif font, whereas the source figure uses a serif font for all text.
The arrows in the source figure are drawn with thick strokes and large heads, whereas the generated arrows are noticeably thinner.
evaluation.notes: Although the screenshot reveals a ReferenceError due to a missing draw initialization, code analysis reveals a remarkably sophisticated and accurate code-execution interactive visualization; the only notable pedagogical flaw is that the default state initializes to the first frame (empty upper boxes) rather than the fully-populated final frame.
action_items: Add `const draw = SVG().addTo('#container').size('100%', '100%');` at the top of the script so it does not throw a ReferenceError on load.

Adjust the initialization logic so that on the first automatic load, the figure jumps to the final frame (`goTo(frames.length - 1)`) to display the complete merge tree, fulfilling the drop-in replacement requirement.
Change the font family for the numbers and 'merge' texts to 'serif' to match the source figure.
Increase the stroke width of the arrows (e.g., width: 5) and scale up the arrowhead marker to better match the bold arrows in the source.
